To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MASSES is a novel evaluation metric for the VQA task that is based on the Majority, Subjectivity and Semantic Similarity of the answers.
the proposed MASSES metric: 1) is effective in providing more fine-grained evaluations, 2) is more informative, and 3) is more reliable than the current metric.

the MA of human annotators is the best source of information for evaluating the performance of a VQA system, that the Subjectivity of the human answers is a key feature for evaluating VQA, and that Semantic Similarity is an essential feature for evaluating the quality of a VQA model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

i) the evaluation of VQA models, and more generally, of models that generate open-ended answers; ii) the evaluation of the quality of VQA datasets, and more generally the quality of open-ended datasets; iii) the evaluation of human annotators and their agreement.

the following aspects: - A new evaluation metric for the VQA task - A quantitative and qualitative analysis of the metric - An empirical evaluation of the metric on the VQA v2.0 dataset - A qualitative evaluation of the metric using the VQA v1.1 dataset
a more fine-grined evaluation of VQA systems, and it provides a new metric that accounts for the MA of the annotators, the S of their responses, and the SES between them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MA, SES and S components of our metric are all valuable and necessary.
the MA, S, and SES of the answers in a dataset are important and should be taken into consideration when evaluating VQA models.
MASSES outperforms standard metrics in terms of accuracy and informativeness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MASSES can be considered a better alternative for evaluating VQA systems.
MASSES is a novel metric for VQA that accounts for the Majority of answers, Subjectivity in the answers, and Semantic Similarty between them.
MASSES can provide a more fine-grined evaluation of the VQA task, and that this metric can be easily extended to other tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard evaluation metric for VQA should be revised.
, when evaluating VQA, the Majority, Subjectivity and Semantic Similarity of the answers should be considered.

, in the VQA task, the evaluation should be performed in a more fine-gruned fashion, accounting for the Subjectivity and Semantic Similarity of the answers, in order to obtain a more accurate assessment of model performance.
